Statement by the director responsible for the business responsibility report, highlighting ESG related challenges, targets and achievements (listed entity has flexibility regarding the placement of this disclosure)

Suraj Estate Developers Limited recognises that responsible urban redevelopment requires effective management of resource consumption, construction waste, site safety and stakeholder expectations. During 2025-26, the Company continued initiatives relating to resource-efficient design, water conservation, reuse of construction materials, waste segregation, workforce safety, community development and responsible customer engagement. While no specific ESG commitments, goals or time-bound targets were set during the year, the Company remains committed to integrating sustainability into decision-making and creating long-term value for all stakeholders.

Yes/No (If yes, then give details of the mechanism in brief)

Suraj Estate Developers Limited has established grievance redressal mechanisms for all employees and workers. HR addresses administrative, leave and payroll concerns, while ethical violations, fraud and Code of Conduct breaches are reported confidentially under the Vigil Mechanism/Whistle Blower Policy and the Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption Policy. Gender discrimination and sexual harassment complaints are handled under the POSH Policy, which covers permanent, contractual and temporary employees, consultants, daily wagers and subcontractor labour. At construction sites, safety, near-miss and labour welfare concerns are reported to the resident Safety Advisor through prescribed HSE reporting tools. Contractors must resolve site-level welfare grievances in line with HSE Contract Guidelines, failing which penalties may be imposed.
